es.title: [Retailing 101 #4] Los últimos 30 metros: Por qué la tienda sigue decidiéndolo todo

segments.src: > Retailing is the final step that moves a product from a business to a person who will actually use it — and that step does far more work than "buy low, sell high."
segments.tr: > El comercio minorista (retailing) es el paso final que traslada un producto de una empresa a la persona que realmente lo usará, y ese paso hace mucho más trabajo que simplemente "comprar barato y vender caro".

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: **Retailing is the sale of goods and services to final consumers for their own personal use — not for resale, and not as an input into another business's product.**
segments.tr: **El comercio minorista es la venta de bienes y servicios a consumidores finales para su uso personal; no para su reventa, y no como un insumo para el producto de otra empresa.**

segments.src: That one sentence carries the whole definition.
segments.tr: Esa única frase contiene toda la definición.

segments.src: When a steel mill sells sheet steel to an automaker, that is not retailing; the steel goes into a car.
segments.tr: Cuando una acería vende láminas de acero a un fabricante de automóviles, eso no es comercio minorista; el acero se convierte en parte de un coche.

segments.src: When you buy a set of floor mats for that car at an auto parts store, that *is* retailing.
segments.tr: Cuando compras un juego de alfombrillas para ese coche en una tienda de repuestos, eso *sí* es comercio minorista.

segments.src: The test is not the size of the seller or whether there's a physical store.
segments.tr: La prueba no es el tamaño del vendedor ni si existe una tienda física.

segments.src: It's who the buyer is and why they're buying.
segments.tr: Es quién es el comprador y por qué está comprando.

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer.
segments.tr: Amazon es un minorista.

segments.src: So is the food truck downtown, the dentist's office, and the barbershop — services count too.
segments.tr: También lo es el camión de comida del centro, el consultorio del dentista y la barbería; los servicios también cuentan.

segments.src: Retail is also the last link in what textbooks call the **distribution channel**: producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer.
segments.tr: El comercio minorista es también el último eslabón en lo que los libros de texto llaman el **canal de distribución**: productor → mayorista → minorista → consumidor.

segments.src: Being last sounds unglamorous, but it's where a specific set of jobs gets done that nobody upstream wants to do:
segments.tr: Ser el último suena poco glamuroso, pero es donde se realiza un conjunto específico de tareas que nadie más arriba en la cadena quiere hacer:

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk.** A roaster ships coffee by the pallet. You want one 12-ounce bag. Someone has to break a pallet into bags, and eat the cost of doing it.
segments.tr: - **Fraccionar al por mayor (Breaking bulk).** Un tostador envía café por palés. Tú quieres una bolsa de 12 onzas. Alguien tiene que dividir un palé en bolsas y asumir el coste de hacerlo.

segments.src: - **Building an assortment.** No manufacturer makes everything you need for dinner. A supermarket assembles 30,000-plus items from thousands of suppliers into one trip.
segments.tr: - **Crear un surtido.** Ningún fabricante hace todo lo que necesitas para cenar. Un supermercado reúne más de 30,000 artículos de miles de proveedores en una sola visita.

segments.src: - **Holding inventory.** The retailer buys and owns the product *before* knowing if it will sell. That's real financial risk, sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: - **Mantener inventario.** El minorista compra y posee el producto *antes* de saber si se venderá. Eso es un riesgo financiero real, acumulando polvo en un estante.

segments.src: - **Providing services.** Store hours, parking, returns, credit, delivery, installation, someone who can answer "will this fit my sink?"
segments.tr: - **Proporcionar servicios.** Horario de tienda, aparcamiento, devoluciones, crédito, entrega, instalación, alguien que pueda responder "¿esto encajará en mi fregadero?"

segments.src: - **Sending information both ways.** Prices and product info flow down to you; scanner data and demand signals flow back up to manufacturers.
segments.tr: - **Enviar información en ambos sentidos.** Los precios y la información del producto fluyen hacia ti; los datos del escáner y las señales de demanda fluyen de vuelta hacia los fabricantes.

segments.src: Economists describe this as creating **utility**: *place* utility (the good is where you are), *time* utility (available when you want it), *possession* utility (ownership transfers easily), and *form* utility (bulk becomes a usable size).
segments.tr: Los economistas describen esto como la creación de **utilidad**: utilidad de *lugar* (el bien está donde tú estás), utilidad de *tiempo* (disponible cuando lo quieres), utilidad de *posesión* (la propiedad se transfiere fácilmente) y utilidad de *forma* (el volumen a granel se convierte en un tamaño utilizable).

segments.src: None of it is free, and all of it is why retail markups exist.
segments.tr: Nada de esto es gratis, y todo ello es la razón por la que existen los márgenes de beneficio minorista.

segments.src: - **1800s — general stores and peddlers.** Small assortments, negotiated prices, credit written in a ledger.
segments.tr: - **1800s — tiendas generales y vendedores ambulantes.** Surtidos pequeños, precios negociados, crédito anotado en un libro de contabilidad.

segments.src: - **1850s–1870s — department stores.** Macy's (1858) and peers introduced fixed prices, wide assortments under one roof, and returns.

segments.tr: - **1872–1893 — venta por catálogo.** Montgomery Ward y luego Sears utilizaron el ferrocarril y el servicio postal para llegar a los hogares agrícolas con un catálogo. ¿Te suena familiar?

segments.src: - **1916 — self-service.** Piggly Wiggly in Memphis let shoppers pick items off shelves themselves, cutting labor cost sharply.
segments.tr: - **1916 — autoservicio.** Piggly Wiggly en Memphis permitió a los compradores tomar los artículos de los estantes ellos mismos, reduciendo drásticamente los costes laborales.

segments.src: - **1930 — supermarkets.** King Kullen in Queens combined self-service, scale, and parking.
segments.tr: - **1930 — supermercados.** King Kullen en Queens combinó autoservicio, escala y aparcamiento.

segments.src: - **1962 — discount stores.** Walmart, Kmart, and Target all opened their first stores that same year, trading service for low price.
segments.tr: - **1962 — tiendas de descuento.** Walmart, Kmart y Target abrieron sus primeras tiendas ese mismo año, intercambiando servicio por precios bajos.

segments.src: - **1980s–1990s — category killers and warehouse clubs.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: go extremely deep in one category, win on price and selection.
segments.tr: - **1980s–1990s — asesinos de categoría y clubes de almacén.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: profundizar extremadamente en una categoría, ganar en precio y selección.

segments.src: - **1994 onward — e-commerce and omnichannel.** Amazon launched in the mid-1990s; today online is roughly 16–17% of total U.S. retail sales, and most large chains blend the two (buy online, pick up in store).
segments.tr: - **1994 en adelante — comercio electrónico y omnicanal.** Amazon se lanzó a mediados de los 90; hoy en día, el comercio en línea representa aproximadamente el 16–17% de las ventas minoristas totales en EE. UU., y la mayoría de las grandes cadenas combinan ambos (comprar en línea, recoger en tienda).

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen en 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. Retailing is selling goods **or services** to the final consumer for personal use — the buyer's purpose defines it, not the seller's size or format.
segments.tr: 1. El comercio minorista es vender bienes **o servicios** al consumidor final para uso personal; el propósito del comprador lo define, no el tamaño o formato del vendedor.

segments.src: 2. Retailers earn their margin by breaking bulk, assembling assortments, carrying inventory risk, providing services, and moving information both directions in the channel.
segments.tr: 2. Los minoristas obtienen su margen fraccionando al por mayor, ensamblando surtidos, asumiendo el riesgo de inventario, proporcionando servicios y moviendo información en ambas direcciones en el canal.

segments.src: 3. Retail formats evolve in a repeating cycle — new entrants attack on price, mature into full-service operators, and get attacked in turn (the Wheel of Retailing).
segments.tr: 3. Los formatos minoristas evolucionan en un ciclo repetitivo: los nuevos participantes atacan por precio, maduran hasta convertirse en operadores de servicio completo y, a su vez, son atacados (la Rueda del Comercio Minorista).

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Retailing** — Selling goods or services to final consumers for personal, non-business use.
segments.tr: - **Comercio minorista (Retailing)** — Venta de bienes o servicios a consumidores finales para uso personal, no comercial.

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The chain of businesses a product passes through from producer to consumer; retail is the last link.
segments.tr: - **Canal de distribución** — La cadena de empresas por las que pasa un producto desde el productor hasta el consumidor; el comercio minorista es el último eslabón.

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk** — Splitting large shipping quantities (pallets, cases) into the small units households actually buy.
segments.tr: - **Fraccionar al por mayor (Breaking bulk)** — Dividir grandes cantidades de envío (palés, cajas) en las pequeñas unidades que los hogares realmente compran.

segments.src: - **Assortment** — The mix a retailer carries, described by *breadth* (how many categories) and *depth* (how many choices within one).
segments.tr: - **Surtido** — La mezcla que lleva un minorista, descrita por su *amplitud* (cuántas categorías) y *profundidad* (cuántas opciones dentro de una).

segments.src: - **Wheel of Retailing** — McNair's theory that formats enter cheap and no-frills, gradually add cost and service, and are displaced by the next low-price entrant.
segments.tr: - **Rueda del Comercio Minorista** — Teoría de McNair de que los formatos entran baratos y sin lujos, añaden gradualmente coste y servicio, y son desplazados por el siguiente participante de bajo precio.

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — Running stores, web, app, and delivery as one integrated system rather than separate businesses.
segments.tr: - **Omnicanal** — Operar tiendas, web, aplicaciones y entregas como un sistema integrado en lugar de negocios separados.

ar.title: [البيع بالتجزئة 101 #4] الأقدام المائة الأخيرة: لماذا يحدد المتجر كل شيء حتى الآن

segments.src: > Retailing is the final step that moves a product from a business to a person who will actually use it — and that step does far more work than "buy low, sell high."
segments.tr: > البيع بالتجزئة هو الخطوة الأخيرة التي تنقل المنتج من النشاط التجاري إلى الشخص الذي سيستخدمه فعلياً - وهذه الخطوة تقوم بعمل أكبر بكثير من مجرد "الشراء بسعر منخفض والبيع بسعر مرتفع".

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: **Retailing is the sale of goods and services to final consumers for their own personal use — not for resale, and not as an input into another business's product.**
segments.tr: **البيع بالتجزئة هو بيع السلع والخدمات للمستهلكين النهائيين للاستخدام الشخصي الخاص بهم - وليس لإعادة البيع، وليس كمدخل لمنتج نشاط تجاري آخر.**

segments.src: That one sentence carries the whole definition.
segments.tr: هذه الجملة الواحدة تحوي التعريف بأكمله.

segments.src: When a steel mill sells sheet steel to an automaker, that is not retailing; the steel goes into a car.
segments.tr: عندما يبيع مصنع صلب صفائح فولاذية لشركة تصنيع سيارات، فهذا ليس بيعاً بالتجزئة؛ فالصلب يدخل في صناعة السيارة.

segments.src: When you buy a set of floor mats for that car at an auto parts store, that *is* retailing.
segments.tr: وعندما تشتري مجموعة من دواسات الأرضية لتلك السيارة من متجر قطع غيار السيارات، فهذا *يعتبر* بيعاً بالتجزئة.

segments.src: The test is not the size of the seller or whether there's a physical store.
segments.tr: المعيار ليس حجم البائع أو ما إذا كان هناك متجر فعلي.

segments.src: It's who the buyer is and why they're buying.
segments.tr: الامر يتعلق بمن هو المشتري ولماذا يشتري.

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer.
segments.tr: أمازون هي شركة تجزئة.

segments.src: So is the food truck downtown, the dentist's office, and the barbershop — services count too.
segments.tr: وكذلك شاحنة الطعام في وسط المدينة، وعيادة طبيب الأسنان، ومحل حلاقة الشعر - فالخدمات تحتسب أيضاً.

segments.src: Retail is also the last link in what textbooks call the **distribution channel**: producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer.
segments.tr: التجزئة هي أيضاً الحلقة الأخيرة فيما تسميه الكتب الدراسية **قناة التوزيع**: المنتج ← تاجر الجملة ← تاجر التجزئة ← المستهلك.

segments.src: Being last sounds unglamorous, but it's where a specific set of jobs gets done that nobody upstream wants to do:
segments.tr: كونها الأخيرة يبدو أمراً غير براق، ولكنه المكان الذي يتم فيه انجاز مجموعة محددة من الوظائف التي لا يريد أي شخص في المراحل السابقة القيام بها:

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk.** A roaster ships coffee by the pallet. You want one 12-ounce bag. Someone has to break a pallet into bags, and eat the cost of doing it.
segments.tr: - **تجزئة الكميات الكبيرة.** يقوم المحمص بشحن القهوة بالمنصات النقالة. أنت تريد كيساً واحداً بوزن 12 أونصة. يجب على شخص ما تفكيك منصة نقالة إلى أكياس، وتحمل تكلفة القيام بذلك.

segments.src: - **Building an assortment.** No manufacturer makes everything you need for dinner. A supermarket assembles 30,000-plus items from thousands of suppliers into one trip.
segments.tr: - **بناء تشكيلة المنتجات.** لا توجد شركة مصنعة تصنع كل ما تحتاجه للعشاء. يجمع السوبر ماركت أكثر من 30,000 صنف من آلاف الموردين في رحلة تسوق واحدة.

segments.src: - **Holding inventory.** The retailer buys and owns the product *before* knowing if it will sell. That's real financial risk, sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: - **الاحتفاظ بالمخزون.** يشتري تاجر التجزئة المنتج ويمتلكه *قبل* معرفة ما إذا كان سيُباع. هذه مخاطرة مالية حقيقية، مستقرة على الرف.

segments.src: - **Providing services.** Store hours, parking, returns, credit, delivery, installation, someone who can answer "will this fit my sink?"
segments.tr: - **توفير الخدمات.** ساعات المتجر، ومواقف السيارات، والمرتجعات، والائتمان، والتوصيل، والتركيب، وشخص يمكنه الإجابة على "هل سيناسب هذا حوض المطبخ الخاص بي؟"

segments.src: - **Sending information both ways.** Prices and product info flow down to you; scanner data and demand signals flow back up to manufacturers.
segments.tr: - **إرسال المعلومات في الاتجاهين.** تنزل الأسعار ومعلومات المنتجات إليك؛ وتصعد بيانات الماسح الضوئي وإشارات الطلب مرة أخرى إلى الشركات المصنعة.

segments.src: Economists describe this as creating **utility**: *place* utility (the good is where you are), *time* utility (available when you want it), *possession* utility (ownership transfers easily), and *form* utility (bulk becomes a usable size).
segments.tr: يصف الاقتصاديون هذا بأنه خلق **المنفعة**: منفعة *المكان* (السلعة موجودة حيث أنت)، ومنفعة *الزمان* (متوفرة عندما تريدها)، ومنفعة *الامتلاك* (تنتقل الملكية بسهولة)، ومنفعة *الشكل* (تتحول الكمية الكبيرة إلى حجم قابل للاستخدام).

segments.src: None of it is free, and all of it is why retail markups exist.
segments.tr: لا شيء من هذا مجاني، وكل ذلك هو سبب وجود هوامش ربح تجارة التجزئة.

segments.src: **How we got here** — a fast tour of U.S.
segments.tr: **كيف وصلنا إلى هنا** - جولة سريعة في تاريخ التجزئة في الولايات المتحدة، لأن كل تنسيق كان إجابة على مشكلة:

segments.src: retail history, because each format was an answer to a problem:
- **1800s — general stores and peddlers.** Small assortments, negotiated prices, credit written in a ledger.
segments.tr: - **القرن التاسع عشر - المتاجر العامة والباعة المتجولون.** تشكيلة صغيرة، أسعار تفاوضية، وائتمان مسجل في دفتر أستاذ.

segments.src: - **1850s–1870s — department stores.** Macy's (1858) and peers introduced fixed prices, wide assortments under one roof, and returns.
segments.tr: - **خمسينيات - سبعينيات القرن التاسع عشر - المتاجر الكبرى.** قدمت ميسيز (1858) وأمثالها أسعاراً ثابتة، وتشكيلات واسعة تحت سقفا واحد، وخدمة الإرجاع.

segments.src: - **1872–1893 — mail order.** Montgomery Ward and then Sears used the railroad and the postal service to reach farm households with a catalog. Sound familiar?
segments.tr: - **1872–1893 - الطلب عبر البريد.** استخدمت شركة مونتغومري وارد ثم سيرز خطوط السكك الحديدية وخدمة البريد للوصول إلى الأسر الزراعية عبر كتالوج. يبدو مألوفاً؟

segments.src: - **1916 — self-service.** Piggly Wiggly in Memphis let shoppers pick items off shelves themselves, cutting labor cost sharply.
segments.tr: - **1916 - الخدمة الذاتية.** سمحت شركة بيغلي ويغلي في ممفيس للمتسوقين باختيار العناصر من الرفوف بأنفسهم، مما أدى إلى خفض تكلفة العمالة بشكل حاد.

segments.src: - **1930 — supermarkets.** King Kullen in Queens combined self-service, scale, and parking.
segments.tr: - **1930 - محلات السوبر ماركت.** جمعت شركة كينج كولين في كوينز بين الخدمة الذاتية، والنطاق الواسع، ومواقف السيارات.

segments.src: - **1962 — discount stores.** Walmart, Kmart, and Target all opened their first stores that same year, trading service for low price.
segments.tr: - **1962 - متاجر الخصم.** افتتحت وول مارت، وكي مارت، وتارجت متاجرهم الأولى في نفس العام، مقابل استبدال الخدمة بالأسعار المنخفضة.

segments.src: - **1980s–1990s — category killers and warehouse clubs.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: go extremely deep in one category, win on price and selection.
segments.tr: - **فترتا الثمانينيات والتسعينيات - محلات الفئة القاتلة والنوادي المستودعات.** هوم ديبوت، بيست باي، كوستكو: التعمق بشكل كبير في فئة واحدة، والفوز عبر السعر والاختيار.

segments.src: - **1994 onward — e-commerce and omnichannel.** Amazon launched in the mid-1990s; today online is roughly 16–17% of total U.S. retail sales, and most large chains blend the two (buy online, pick up in store).
segments.tr: - **1994 فصاعداً - التجارة الإلكترونية والتجارة متعددة القنوات.** أطلقت أمازون في منتصف التسعينيات؛ واليوم تشكل التجارة عبر الإنترنت ما يقريب من 16-17٪ من إجمالي مبيعات التجزئة في الولايات المتحدة، وتدمج معظم السلاسل الكبيرة بين الاثنين (الشراء عبر الإنترنت، والاستلام من المتجر).

segments.src: Notice the pattern.
segments.tr: لاحظ النمط.

segments.src: Malcolm McNair called it the **Wheel of Retailing**: new formats usually enter as low-price, low-margin, no-frills operators, gradually add services and costs as they mature, and thereby open the low end for the next disruptor.
segments.tr: أطلق مالكولم ماكنير على هذا اسم **عجلة تجارة التجزئة**: عادة ما تدخل التنسيقات الجديدة كجهات تشغيل ذات أسعار منخفضة، وهوامش ربح منخفضة، وبدون خدمات إضافية، وتضيف تدريجياً الخدمات والتكاليف مع نضوجها، وبذلك تفتح الجانب المنخفض للمخرب التالي.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: 1. البيع بالتجزئة هو بيع السلع **أو الخدمات** للمستهلك النهائي للاستخدام الشخصي - هدف المشتري يحدده، وليس حجم البائع أو تنسيقه.

segments.src: 1. Retailing is selling goods **or services** to the final consumer for personal use — the buyer's purpose defines it, not the seller's size or format.
segments.tr: 2. يکسب تجار التجزئة هامش ربحهم من خلال تفكيك الكميات الكبيرة، وتجميع التشكيلات، وتحمل مخاطر المخزون، وتوفير الخدمات، ونقل المعلومات في كلا الاتجاهين في القناة.

fr.title: [Retailing 101 #4] Les 100 derniers pieds : Pourquoi le magasin décide encore de tout

segments.src: > Retailing is the final step that moves a product from a business to a person who will actually use it — and that step does far more work than "buy low, sell high."
segments.tr: > La vente au détail est la dernière étape qui fait passer un produit d'une entreprise à une personne qui va réellement l'utiliser — et cette étape fait bien plus que simplement « acheter bas, vendre haut ».

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept du jour

segments.src: **Retailing is the sale of goods and services to final consumers for their own personal use — not for resale, and not as an input into another business's product.**
segments.tr: **La vente au détail est la vente de biens et de services aux consommateurs finaux pour leur propre usage personnel — et non pour la revente, ni comme intrant dans le produit d'une autre entreprise.**

segments.src: That one sentence carries the whole definition.
segments.tr: Cette seule phrase contient toute la définition.

segments.src: When a steel mill sells sheet steel to an automaker, that is not retailing; the steel goes into a car.
segments.tr: Lorsqu'une aciérie vend des tôle d'acier à un constructeur automobile, il ne s'agit pas de vente au détail ; l'acier entre dans la composition d'une voiture.

segments.src: When you buy a set of floor mats for that car at an auto parts store, that *is* retailing.
segments.tr: Lorsque vous achetez un jeu de tapis de sol pour cette voiture dans un magasin de pièces auto, *c'est* de la vente au détail.

segments.src: The test is not the size of the seller or whether there's a physical store.
segments.tr: Le critère n'est pas la taille du vendeur ou l'existence d'un magasin physique.

segments.src: It's who the buyer is and why they're buying.
segments.tr: C'est qui est l'acheteur et pourquoi il achète.

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer.
segments.tr: Amazon est un détaillant.

segments.src: So is the food truck downtown, the dentist's office, and the barbershop — services count too.
segments.tr: Le camion-restaurant du centre-ville, le cabinet dentaire et le salon de coiffure le sont aussi — les services comptent également.

segments.src: Retail is also the last link in what textbooks call the **distribution channel**: producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer.
segments.tr: Le commerce de détail est également le dernier maillon de ce que les manuels appellent le **canal de distribution** : producteur → grossiste → détaillant → consommateur.

segments.src: Being last sounds unglamorous, but it's where a specific set of jobs gets done that nobody upstream wants to do:
segments.tr: Être le dernier peut sembler peu glamour, mais c'est là que s'exécute un ensemble précis de tâches que personne en amont ne veut faire :

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk.** A roaster ships coffee by the pallet. You want one 12-ounce bag. Someone has to break a pallet into bags, and eat the cost of doing it.
segments.tr: - **Le fractionnement. ** Un torréfacteur expédie du café par palette. Vous voulez un sachet de 12 onces. Quelqu'un doit diviser une palette en sachets et assumer le coût de cette opération.

segments.src: - **Building an assortment.** No manufacturer makes everything you need for dinner. A supermarket assembles 30,000-plus items from thousands of suppliers into one trip.
segments.tr: - **La constitution d'un assortiment. ** Aucun fabricant ne fabrique tout ce dont vous avez besoin pour le dîner. Un supermarché rassemble plus de 30 000 articles provenant de milliers de fournisseurs en un seul voyage.

segments.src: - **Holding inventory.** The retailer buys and owns the product *before* knowing if it will sell. That's real financial risk, sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: - **La détention de stocks. ** Le détaillant achète et possède le produit *avant* de savoir s'il se vendra. C'est un réel risque financier, assis sur une étagère.

segments.src: - **Providing services.** Store hours, parking, returns, credit, delivery, installation, someone who can answer "will this fit my sink?"
segments.tr: - **La fourniture de services. ** Heures d'ouverture, stationnement, retours, crédit, livraison, installation, quelqu'un qui peut répondre à « est-ce que ça va aller dans mon évier ? »

segments.src: - **Sending information both ways.** Prices and product info flow down to you; scanner data and demand signals flow back up to manufacturers.
segments.tr: - **L'envoi d'informations dans les deux sens. ** Les prix et les informations sur les produits descendent vers vous ; les données des scanners et les signaux de demande remontent vers les fabricants.

segments.src: Economists describe this as creating **utility**: *place* utility (the good is where you are), *time* utility (available when you want it), *possession* utility (ownership transfers easily), and *form* utility (bulk becomes a usable size).
segments.tr: Les économistes décrivent cela comme la création d'une **utilité** : l'utilité de *lieu* (le bien est là où vous êtes), l'utilité de *temps* (disponible quand vous le voulez), l'utilité de *possession* (la propriété se transfère facilement) et l'utilité de *forme* (le vrac devient une taille utilisable).

segments.src: None of it is free, and all of it is why retail markups exist.
segments.tr: Rien de tout cela n'est gratuit, et tout cela explique l'existence des marges bénéficiaires dans le commerce de détail.

segments.src: **How we got here** — a fast tour of U.S.
segments.tr: **Comment nous en sommes arrivés là** — un rapide tour d'horizon de l'histoire de la vente au détail aux États-Unis,

segments.src: retail history, because each format was an answer to a problem:
segments.tr: car chaque format était une réponse à un problème :

segments.src: - **1800s — general stores and peddlers.** Small assortments, negotiated prices, credit written in a ledger.
segments.tr: - **Années 1800 — magasins généraux et colporteurs. ** Petits assortiments, prix négociés, crédit inscrit dans un grand livre.

segments.src: - **1850s–1870s — department stores.** Macy's (1858) and peers introduced fixed prices, wide assortments under one roof, and returns.
segments.tr: - **Années 1850-1870 — grands magasins. ** Macy's (1858) et ses pairs ont introduit des prix fixes, de larges assortiments sous un même toit et les retours.

segments.src: - **1872–1893 — mail order.** Montgomery Ward and then Sears used the railroad and the postal service to reach farm households with a catalog. Sound familiar?
segments.tr: - **1872-1893 — vente par correspondance. ** Montgomery Ward puis Sears ont utilisé le chemin de fer et le service postal pour atteindre les ménages ruraux avec un catalogue. Ça vous rappelle quelque chose ?

segments.src: - **1916 — self-service.** Piggly Wiggly in Memphis let shoppers pick items off shelves themselves, cutting labor cost sharply.
segments.tr: - **1916 — libre-service. ** Piggly Wiggly à Memphis a permis aux acheteurs de prendre eux-mêmes les articles sur les étagères, réduisant fortement les coûts de main-d'œuvre.

segments.src: - **1930 — supermarkets.** King Kullen in Queens combined self-service, scale, and parking.
segments.tr: - **1930 — supermarchés. ** King Kullen dans le Queens a combiné le libre-service, l'échelle et le stationnement.

segments.src: - **1962 — discount stores.** Walmart, Kmart, and Target all opened their first stores that same year, trading service for low price.
segments.tr: - **1962 — magasins à prix discount. ** Walmart, Kmart et Target ont tous ouvert leurs premiers magasins la même année, troquant le service contre des prix bas.

segments.src: - **1980s–1990s — category killers and warehouse clubs.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: go extremely deep in one category, win on price and selection.
segments.tr: - **Années 1980-1990 — grandes surfaces spécialisées et clubs-entrepôts. ** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco : aller extrêmement loin dans une catégorie, gagner sur les prix et le choix.

segments.src: - **1994 onward — e-commerce and omnichannel.** Amazon launched in the mid-1990s; today online is roughly 16–17% of total U.S. retail sales, and most large chains blend the two (buy online, pick up in store).
segments.tr: - **À partir de 1994 — commerce électronique et omnicanal. ** Amazon a été lancé au milieu des années 1990 ; aujourd'hui, le commerce en ligne représente environ 16 à 17 % du total des ventes au détail aux États-Unis, et la plupart des grandes chaînes combinent les deux (achat en ligne, retrait en magasin).

segments.src: Notice the pattern.
segments.tr: Remarquez le schéma.

segments.src: Malcolm McNair called it the **Wheel of Retailing**: new formats usually enter as low-price, low-margin, no-frills operators, gradually add services and costs as they mature, and thereby open the low end for the next disruptor.
segments.tr: Malcolm McNair a appelé cela la **Roue de la vente au détail** : les nouveaux formats entrent généralement en tant qu'opérateurs à bas prix, à faible marge et sans fioritures, ajoutent progressivement des services et des coûts à mesure qu'ils mûritent, et ouvrent ainsi le bas de gamme pour le prochain perturbateur.

segments.src: Discounters did it to department stores.
segments.tr: Les discounters l'ont fait aux grands magasins.

segments.src: Online did it to discounters.
segments.tr: Le Web l'a fait aux discounters.

segments.src: Something will do it to online.
segments.tr: Quelque chose le fera au Web.

segments.src: The beans were grown in Colombia, sold in 60-kilogram sacks, shipped in a container, roasted in a facility that runs in thousand-pound batches, and trucked to a distribution center on a pallet holding a couple hundred bags.
segments.tr: Les grains ont été cultivés en Colombie, vendus en sacs de 60 kilogrammes, expédiés dans un conteneur, torréfiés dans une usine qui fonctionne par lots de mille livres, et acheminés par camion vers un centre de distribution sur une palette contenant quelques centaines de sacs.

segments.src: The retailer bought that pallet outright — before knowing whether Columbus would want medium roast this month.
segments.tr: Le détaillant a acheté cette palette comptant — avant de savoir si Columbus voudrait du café torréfié moyen ce mois-ci.

segments.src: It broke the pallet into single bags, put them on a shelf next to eleven competing brands plus whole-bean, ground, and decaf options, kept the lights and the doors open until 10 p.m., took your card, and would have refunded you without argument if the bag was stale.
segments.tr: Il a divisé la palette en sachets individuels, les a mis sur une étagère à côté de onze marques concurrentes ainsi que des options de grains entiers, moulus et décaféinés, a gardé les lumières et les portes ouvertes jusqu'à 22h, a pris votre carte et vous aurait remboursé sans discuter si le sachet était éventé.

segments.src: The gap between what the store paid and what you paid mostly went to rent, wages, refrigeration, trucks, shrink, and unsold inventory — that is, to the cost of getting one bag of coffee within walking distance of your kitchen at a moment you chose.

pt.title: [Retailing 101 #4] Os Últimos 30 Metros: Por que a Loja Ainda Decide Tudo

segments.src: > Retailing is the final step that moves a product from a business to a person who will actually use it — and that step does far more work than "buy low, sell high."
segments.tr: > O varejo é a etapa final que move um produto de uma empresa para uma pessoa que realmente vai usá-lo — e essa etapa faz muito mais do que "comprar barato, vender caro".

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: **Retailing is the sale of goods and services to final consumers for their own personal use — not for resale, and not as an input into another business's product.**
segments.tr: **O varejo é a venda de bens e serviços aos consumidores finais para seu próprio uso pessoal — não para revenda e não como insumo para o produto de outra empresa.**

segments.src: That one sentence carries the whole definition.
segments.tr: Essa única frase carrega toda a definição.

segments.src: When a steel mill sells sheet steel to an automaker, that is not retailing; the steel goes into a car.
segments.tr: Quando uma siderúrgica vende chapa de aço para uma montadora, isso não é varejo; o aço vai para dentro de um carro.

segments.src: When you buy a set of floor mats for that car at an auto parts store, that *is* retailing.
segments.tr: Quando você compra um jogo de tapetes para esse carro em uma loja de autopeças, isso *é* varejo.

segments.src: The test is not the size of the seller or whether there's a physical store.
segments.tr: O teste não é o tamanho do vendedor ou se há uma loja física.

segments.src: It's who the buyer is and why they're buying.
segments.tr: É quem é o comprador e por que ele está comprando.

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer.
segments.tr: A Amazon é uma varejista.

segments.src: So is the food truck downtown, the dentist's office, and the barbershop — services count too.
segments.tr: O caminhão de comida na rua, o consultório dentário e a barbearia também — serviços contam também.

segments.src: Retail is also the last link in what textbooks call the **distribution channel**: producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer.
segments.tr: O varejo também é o último elo no que os livros didáticos chamam de **canal de distribuição**: produtor → atacadista → varejista → consumidor.

segments.src: Being last sounds unglamorous, but it's where a specific set of jobs gets done that nobody upstream wants to do:
segments.tr: Ser o último soa pouco glamoroso, mas é onde um conjunto específico de tarefas é realizado que ninguém a montante quer fazer:

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk.** A roaster ships coffee by the pallet. You want one 12-ounce bag. Someone has to break a pallet into bags, and eat the cost of doing it.
segments.tr: - **Fracionamento de grandes volumes (Breaking bulk).** Um torrefador despacha café por palete. Você quer um pacote de 340 gramas. Alguém tem que dividir um palete em pacotes e arcar com o custo de fazer isso.

segments.src: - **Building an assortment.** No manufacturer makes everything you need for dinner. A supermarket assembles 30,000-plus items from thousands of suppliers into one trip.
segments.tr: - **Montagem de sortimento.** Nenhum fabricante faz tudo o que você precisa para o jantar. Um supermercado reúne mais de 30.000 itens de milhares de fornecedores em uma única viagem.

segments.src: - **Holding inventory.** The retailer buys and owns the product *before* knowing if it will sell. That's real financial risk, sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: - **Manutenção de estoque.** O varejista compra e é dono do produto *antes* de saber se ele vai vender. Isso é risco financeiro real, parado na prateleira.

segments.src: - **Providing services.** Store hours, parking, returns, credit, delivery, installation, someone who can answer "will this fit my sink?"
segments.tr: - **Prestação de serviços.** Horário de funcionamento, estacionamento, devoluções, crédito, entrega, instalação, alguém que possa responder "isso cabe na minha pia?"

segments.src: - **Sending information both ways.** Prices and product info flow down to you; scanner data and demand signals flow back up to manufacturers.
segments.tr: - **Envio de informações em ambas as direções.** Preços e informações do produto fluem para você; dados de scanner e sinais de demanda fluem de volta para os fabricantes.

segments.src: Economists describe this as creating **utility**: *place* utility (the good is where you are), *time* utility (available when you want it), *possession* utility (ownership transfers easily), and *form* utility (bulk becomes a usable size).
segments.tr: Os economistas descrevem isso como a criação de **utilidade**: utilidade de *lugar* (o bem está onde você está), utilidade de *tempo* (disponível quando você quer), utilidade de *posse* (a propriedade é transferida facilmente) e utilidade de *forma* (o volume a granel se torna um tamanho utilizable).

segments.src: None of it is free, and all of it is why retail markups exist.
segments.tr: Nada disso é de graça, e tudo isso é o motivo pelo qual existem as margens de lucro do varejo.

segments.src: **How we got here** — a fast tour of U.S.
segments.tr: **Como chegamos aqui** — um rápido tour pela história do varejo dos EUA,

segments.src: retail history, because each format was an answer to a problem:
segments.tr: porque cada formato era uma resposta a um problema:

segments.src: - **1800s — general stores and peddlers.** Small assortments, negotiated prices, credit written in a ledger.
segments.tr: - **Anos 1800 — lojas gerais e mascates.** Sortimentos pequenos, preços negociados, crédito anotado em um livro-razão.

segments.src: - **1850s–1870s — department stores.** Macy's (1858) and peers introduced fixed prices, wide assortments under one roof, and returns.
segments.tr: - **Décadas de 1850 a 1870 — lojas de departamento.** A Macy's (1858) e concorrentes introduziram preços fixos, amplos sortimentos sob o mesmo teto e devoluções.

segments.src: - **1872–1893 — mail order.** Montgomery Ward and then Sears used the railroad and the postal service to reach farm households with a catalog. Sound familiar?
segments.tr: - **1872–1893 — venda por catálogo.** Montgomery Ward e depois a Sears usaram a ferrovia e o serviço postal para alcançar lares agrícolas com um catálogo. Parece familiar?

segments.src: - **1916 — self-service.** Piggly Wiggly in Memphis let shoppers pick items off shelves themselves, cutting labor cost sharply.
segments.tr: - **1916 — autosserviço.** A Piggly Wiggly em Memphis permitiu que os compradores escolhessem itens das prateleiras sozinhos, cortando drasticamente o custo de mão de obra.

segments.src: - **1930 — supermarkets.** King Kullen in Queens combined self-service, scale, and parking.
segments.tr: - **1930 — supermercados.** O King Kullen no Queens combinou autosserviço, escala e estacionamento.

segments.src: - **1962 — discount stores.** Walmart, Kmart, and Target all opened their first stores that same year, trading service for low price.
segments.tr: - **1962 — lojas de desconto.** Walmart, Kmart e Target abriram suas primeiras lojas no mesmo ano, trocando serviço por preço baixo.

segments.src: - **1980s–1990s — category killers and warehouse clubs.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: go extremely deep in one category, win on price and selection.
segments.tr: - **Décadas de 1980 a 1990 — category killers e clubes de atacado.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: ir extremamente fundo em uma categoria, vencer pelo preço e seleção.

segments.src: - **1994 onward — e-commerce and omnichannel.** Amazon launched in the mid-1990s; today online is roughly 16–17% of total U.S. retail sales, and most large chains blend the two (buy online, pick up in store).
segments.tr: - **1994 em diante — e-commerce e omnichannel.** A Amazon foi lançada em meados dos anos 90; hoje o online representa cerca de 16-17% das vendas totais do varejo dos EUA, e a maioria das grandes redes mescla os dois (comprar online, retirar na loja).

segments.src: Notice the pattern.
segments.tr: Observe o padrão.

segments.src: Malcolm McNair called it the **Wheel of Retailing**: new formats usually enter as low-price, low-margin, no-frills operators, gradually add services and costs as they mature, and thereby open the low end for the next disruptor.
segments.tr: Malcolm McNair chamou isso de **Roda do Varejo**: novos formatos geralmente entram como operadores de baixo preço, baixa margem e sem luxos, gradualmente adicionam serviços e custos à medida que amadurecem e, com isso, abrem a extremidade inferior para o próximo disruptor.

segments.src: Discounters did it to department stores.
segments.tr: Os descontistas fizeram isso com as lojas de departamento.

segments.src: Online did it to discounters.
segments.tr: O online fez isso com os descontistas.

segments.src: Something will do it to online.
segments.tr: Algo fará isso com o online.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Quotidiana

segments.src: You pay **$12.99** for a 12-ounce bag of coffee at a Kroger in Columbus on a Sunday evening.
segments.tr: Você paga **$12.99** por um pacote de 340 gramas de café em um Kroger em Columbus em um domingo à noite.

segments.src: It feels like a small transaction.
segments.tr: Parece uma transação pequena.

segments.src: Count what the store actually did for that price.
segments.tr: Conte o que a loja realmente fez por esse preço.

segments.src: The beans were grown in Colombia, sold in 60-kilogram sacks, shipped in a container, roasted in a facility that runs in thousand-pound batches, and trucked to a distribution center on a pallet holding a couple hundred bags.
segments.tr: Os grãos foram cultivados na Colômbia, vendidos em sacas de 60 quilos, despachados em um contêiner, torrados em uma instalação que opera em lotes de mil libras e transportados de caminhão para um centro de distribuição em um palete contendo algumas centenas de pacotes.

segments.src: The retailer bought that pallet outright — before knowing whether Columbus would want medium roast this month.
segments.tr: O varejista comprou esse palete integralmente — antes de saber se Columbus iria querer torra média este mês.

segments.src: It broke the pallet into single bags, put them on a shelf next to eleven competing brands plus whole-bean, ground, and decaf options, kept the lights and the doors open until 10 p.m., took your card, and would have refunded you without argument if the bag was stale.
segments.tr: Ele dividiu o palete em pacotes individuais, colocou-os em uma prateleira ao lado de onze marcas concorrentes, além de opções em grãos, moído e descafeinado, manteve as luzes e as portas abertas até as 22h, aceitou seu cartão e teria reembolsado você sem argumentar se o café estivesse velho.

segments.src: For all of that, a typical U.S.
segments.tr: Por tudo isso, um supermercado típico dos EUA

segments.src: supermarket keeps roughly **1 to 3 cents of net profit per dollar** of sales.
segments.tr: mantém aproximadamente **1 a 3 centavos de lucro líquido por dólar** de vendas.

segments.src: Groceries are one of the thinnest-margin businesses in the country.
segments.tr: Os supermercados são um dos negócios com margens mais estreitas do país.

segments.src: The gap between what the store paid and what you paid mostly went to rent, wages, refrigeration, trucks, shrink, and unsold inventory — that is, to the cost of getting one bag of coffee within walking distance of your kitchen at a moment you chose.
segments.tr: A diferença entre o que a loja pagou e o que você pagou foi principalmente para aluguel, salários, refrigeração, caminhões, perdas e estoque não vendido — ou seja, para o custo de colocar um pacote de café a uma distância que se possa caminhar da sua cozinha no momento que você escolheu.

segments.src: That's the honest answer to "why not just buy direct from the roaster?"
segments.tr: Essa é a resposta honesta para "por que não comprar direto do torrefador?"

segments.src: You can.
segments.tr: Você pode.

segments.src: You'll wait three days, pay shipping, and commit before tasting it.
segments.tr: Você vai esperar três dias, pagar frete e se comprometer antes de provar.

segments.src: The store's price includes the option of changing your mind.
segments.tr: O preço da loja inclui a opção de mudar de ideia.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Recapitulação em 3 Linhas

segments.src: 1. Retailing is selling goods **or services** to the final consumer for personal use — the buyer's purpose defines it, not the seller's size or format.
segments.tr: 1. O varejo é a venda de bens **ou serviços** ao consumidor final para uso pessoal — o propósito do comprador o define, não o tamanho ou formato do vendedor.

segments.src: 2. Retailers earn their margin by breaking bulk, assembling assortments, carrying inventory risk, providing services, and moving information both directions in the channel.
segments.tr: 2. Os varejistas ganham sua margem fracionando volumes, montando sortimentos, assumindo riscos de estoque, fornecendo serviços e movendo informações em ambas as direções no canal.

segments.src: 3. Retail formats evolve in a repeating cycle — new entrants attack on price, mature into full-service operators, and get attacked in turn (the Wheel of Retailing).
segments.tr: 3. Os formatos de varejo evoluem em um ciclo repetitivo — novos entrantes atacam pelo preço, amadurecem como operadores de serviço completo e são atacados por sua vez (a Roda do Varejo).

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Retailing** — Selling goods or services to final consumers for personal, non-business use.
segments.tr: - **Varejo (Retailing)** — Venda de bens ou serviços aos consumidores finais para uso pessoal e não comercial.

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The chain of businesses a product passes through from producer to consumer; retail is the last link.
segments.tr: - **Canal de distribuição** — A cadeia de empresas pela qual um produto passa do produtor ao consumidor; o varejo é o último elo.

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk** — Splitting large shipping quantities (pallets, cases) into the small units households actually buy.
segments.tr: - **Fracionamento de grandes volumes (Breaking bulk)** — Dividir grandes quantidades de envio (paletes, caixas) nas pequenas unidades que os domicílios realmente compram.

segments.src: - **Assortment** — The mix a retailer carries, described by *breadth* (how many categories) and *depth* (how many choices within one).
segments.tr: - **Sortimento (Assortment)** - A mistura que um varejista carrega, descrita pela *amplitude* (quantas categorias) e *profundidade* (quantas opções dentro de uma).

segments.src: - **Wheel of Retailing** — McNair's theory that formats enter cheap and no-frills, gradually add cost and service, and are displaced by the next low-price entrant.
segments.tr: - **Roda do Varejo (Wheel of Retailing)** — A teoria de McNair de que os formatos entram baratos e sem luxos, adicionam gradualmente custo e serviço, e são deslocados pelo próximo entrante de baixo preço.

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — Running stores, web, app, and delivery as one integrated system rather than separate businesses.
segments.tr: - **Omnichannel** — Operar lojas, web, aplicativo e entrega como um sistema integrado em vez de negócios separados.

segments.tr: *Respostas: **1) c** — o aço é um insumo para o produto de outra empresa, portanto é uma transação B2B, não varejo; note que (a) e (d) são serviços e ainda contam como varejo.

segments.src: **2) X (False)** — the margin pays for bulk-breaking, assortment, inventory risk, store hours, and returns; a supermarket's net profit is typically only about 1–3 cents on the dollar.
segments.tr: **2) X (Falso)** — a margem paga pelo fracionamento de volume, sortimento, risco de estoque, horário de funcionamento e devoluções; o lucro líquido de um supermercado é tipicamente de apenas cerca de 1 a 3 centavos por dólar.

segments.src: **3) b** — low-price, low-service entry is the first turn of the wheel; discount stores in 1962 and e-commerce in the late 1990s both followed this path.*
segments.tr: **3) b** — a entrada com baixo preço e baixo serviço é a primeira volta da roda; as lojas de desconto em 1962 e o e-commerce no final dos anos 90 seguiram esse caminho.*

segments.src: > Retailing is the final step that moves a product from a business to a person who will actually use it — and that step does far more work than "buy low, sell high."
segments.tr: > Ritel adalah langkah akhir yang memindahkan produk dari bisnis ke orang yang benar-benar akan menggunakannya — dan langkah tersebut melakukan pekerjaan yang jauh lebih banyak daripada "beli rendah, jual tinggi."

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: **Retailing is the sale of goods and services to final consumers for their own personal use — not for resale, and not as an input into another business's product.**
segments.tr: **Ritel adalah penjualan barang dan jasa kepada konsumen akhir untuk penggunaan pribadi mereka sendiri — bukan untuk dijual kembali, dan bukan sebagai masukan ke dalam produk bisnis lain.**

segments.src: That one sentence carries the whole definition.
segments.tr: Satu kalimat itu memuat seluruh definisi.

segments.src: When a steel mill sells sheet steel to an automaker, that is not retailing; the steel goes into a car.
segments.tr: Ketika pabrik baja menjual lembaran baja ke produsen mobil, itu bukan ritel; baja tersebut masuk ke dalam mobil.

segments.src: When you buy a set of floor mats for that car at an auto parts store, that *is* retailing.
segments.tr: Ketika Anda membeli seperangkat karpet lantai untuk mobil tersebut di toko suku cadang mobil, itu *adalah* ritel.

segments.src: The test is not the size of the seller or whether there's a physical store.
segments.tr: Ujiannya bukan pada ukuran penjual atau apakah ada toko fisik.

segments.src: It's who the buyer is and why they're buying.
segments.tr: Ini tentang siapa pembelinya dan mengapa mereka membeli.

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer.
segments.tr: Amazon adalah pengecer.

segments.src: So is the food truck downtown, the dentist's office, and the barbershop — services count too.
segments.tr: Begitu juga truk makanan di pusat kota, kantor dokter gigi, dan tempat pangkas rambut — layanan juga dihitung.

segments.src: Retail is also the last link in what textbooks call the **distribution channel**: producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer.
segments.tr: Ritel juga merupakan tautan terakhir dalam apa yang disebut oleh buku teks sebagai **saluran distribusi**: produsen → grosir → pengecer → konsumen.

segments.src: Being last sounds unglamorous, but it's where a specific set of jobs gets done that nobody upstream wants to do:
segments.tr: Menjadi yang terakhir terdengar tidak glamor, tetapi di sanalah serangkaian pekerjaan tertentu diselesaikan yang tidak ingin dilakukan oleh siapa pun di hulu:

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk.** A roaster ships coffee by the pallet. You want one 12-ounce bag. Someone has to break a pallet into bags, and eat the cost of doing it.
segments.tr: - **Memecah grosir (Breaking bulk).** Seorang pemanggang mengirimkan kopi berdasarkan palet. Anda ingin satu kantong 12 ons. Seseorang harus memecah palet menjadi beberapa kantong, dan menanggung biaya melakukannya.

segments.src: - **Building an assortment.** No manufacturer makes everything you need for dinner. A supermarket assembles 30,000-plus items from thousands of suppliers into one trip.
segments.tr: - **Membangun berbagai macam produk (Building an assortment).** Tidak ada produsen yang membuat semua yang Anda butuhkan untuk makan malam. Sebuah supermarket mengumpulkan lebih dari 30.000 item dari ribuan pemasok menjadi satu perjalanan.

segments.src: - **Holding inventory.** The retailer buys and owns the product *before* knowing if it will sell. That's real financial risk, sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: - **Menyimpan inventaris (Holding inventory).** Pengecer membeli dan memiliki produk *sebelum* mengetahui apakah produk itu akan terjual. Itu adalah risiko finansial nyata, yang ada di rak.

segments.src: - **Providing services.** Store hours, parking, returns, credit, delivery, installation, someone who can answer "will this fit my sink?"
segments.tr: - **Menyediakan layanan.** Jam buka toko, parkir, pengembalian, kredit, pengiriman, pemasangan, seseorang yang dapat menjawab "apakah ini akan pas di wastafel saya?"

segments.src: - **Sending information both ways.** Prices and product info flow down to you; scanner data and demand signals flow back up to manufacturers.
segments.tr: - **Mengirimkan informasi dua arah.** Harga dan informasi produk mengalir ke bawah kepada Anda; data pemindai dan sinyal permintaan mengalir kembali ke produsen.

segments.src: Economists describe this as creating **utility**: *place* utility (the good is where you are), *time* utility (available when you want it), *possession* utility (ownership transfers easily), and *form* utility (bulk becomes a usable size).
segments.tr: Ekonom menggambarkan ini sebagai menciptakan **utilitas**: utilitas *tempat* (barang berada di tempat Anda berada), utilitas *waktu* (tersedia saat Anda menginginkannya), utilitas *kepemilikan* (kepemilikan berpindah dengan mudah), dan utilitas *bentuk* (ukuran besar menjadi ukuran yang dapat digunakan).

segments.src: None of it is free, and all of it is why retail markups exist.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang gratis, dan semua itu adalah alasan mengapa kenaikan harga ritel ada.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: You pay **$12.99** for a 12-ounce bag of coffee at a Kroger in Columbus on a Sunday evening.
segments.tr: Anda membayar **$12.99** untuk sekantong kopi 12 ons di Kroger di Columbus pada Minggu malam.

segments.src: It feels like a small transaction.
segments.tr: Rasanya seperti transaksi kecil.

segments.src: Count what the store actually did for that price.
segments.tr: Hitung apa yang sebenarnya dilakukan toko untuk harga tersebut.

segments.src: The beans were grown in Colombia, sold in 60-kilogram sacks, shipped in a container, roasted in a facility that runs in thousand-pound batches, and trucked to a distribution center on a pallet holding a couple hundred bags.
segments.tr: Biji kopi ditanam di Kolombia, dijual dalam karung 60 kilogram, dikirim dalam kontainer, dipanggang di fasilitas yang berjalan dalam batch seribu pon, dan diangkut dengan truk ke pusat distribusi pada palet yang menampung beberapa ratus kantong.

segments.src: The retailer bought that pallet outright — before knowing whether Columbus would want medium roast this month.
segments.tr: Pengecer membeli palet itu secara langsung — sebelum mengetahui apakah Columbus menginginkan panggangan sedang bulan ini.

segments.src: It broke the pallet into single bags, put them on a shelf next to eleven competing brands plus whole-bean, ground, and decaf options, kept the lights and the doors open until 10 p.m., took your card, and would have refunded you without argument if the bag was stale.
segments.tr: Ini memecah palet menjadi kantong tunggal, menempatkannya di rak di sebelah sebelas merek yang bersaing ditambah biji utuh, bubuk, dan pilihan tanpa kafein, menjaga lampu dan pintu tetap terbuka sampai jam 10 malam, mengambil kartu Anda, dan akan mengembalikan uang Anda tanpa argumen jika kantongnya basi.

segments.src: For all of that, a typical U.S.
segments.tr: Untuk semua itu, khas A.S.

segments.tr: supermarket menyimpan sekitar **1 hingga 3 sen laba bersih per dolar** dari penjualan.

segments.src: Groceries are one of the thinnest-margin businesses in the country.
segments.tr: Bahan makanan adalah salah satu bisnis dengan margin paling tipis di negara ini.

segments.src: The gap between what the store paid and what you paid mostly went to rent, wages, refrigeration, trucks, shrink, and unsold inventory — that is, to the cost of getting one bag of coffee within walking distance of your kitchen at a moment you chose.
segments.tr: Kesenjangan antara apa yang dibayar toko dan apa yang Anda bayar sebagian besar masuk ke sewa, upah, pendinginan, truk, penyusutan, dan inventaris yang tidak terjual — yaitu, untuk biaya mendapatkan sekantong kopi dalam jarak berjalan kaki dari dapur Anda pada saat yang Anda pilih.

segments.src: That's the honest answer to "why not just buy direct from the roaster?"

segments.src: The store's price includes the option of changing your mind.
segments.tr: Harga toko termasuk opsi untuk mengubah pikiran Anda.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan 3 Baris

segments.src: 1. Retailing is selling goods **or services** to the final consumer for personal use — the buyer's purpose defines it, not the seller's size or format.
segments.tr: 1. Ritel adalah menjual barang **atau jasa** kepada konsumen akhir untuk penggunaan pribadi — tujuan pembeli mendefinisikannya, bukan ukuran atau format penjual.

segments.src: 2. Retailers earn their margin by breaking bulk, assembling assortments, carrying inventory risk, providing services, and moving information both directions in the channel.
segments.tr: 2. Pengecer mendapatkan margin mereka dengan memecah jumlah besar, merakit bermacam-macam, menanggung risiko inventaris, menyediakan layanan, dan memindahkan informasi dua arah di saluran.

segments.src: 3. Retail formats evolve in a repeating cycle — new entrants attack on price, mature into full-service operators, and get attacked in turn (the Wheel of Retailing).
segments.tr: 3. Format ritel berkembang dalam siklus berulang — pendatang baru menyerang pada harga, matang menjadi operator layanan penuh, dan diserang pada gilirannya (Roda Ritel).

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Retailing** — Selling goods or services to final consumers for personal, non-business use.
segments.tr: - **Ritel (Retailing)** — Menjual barang atau jasa kepada konsumen akhir untuk penggunaan pribadi, non-bisnis.

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The chain of businesses a product passes through from producer to consumer; retail is the last link.
segments.tr: - **Saluran distribusi (Distribution channel)** — Rantai bisnis yang dilalui produk dari produsen ke konsumen; ritel adalah tautan terakhir.

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk** — Splitting large shipping quantities (pallets, cases) into the small units households actually buy.
segments.tr: - **Memecah grosir (Breaking bulk)** — Membagi jumlah pengiriman besar (palet, kotak) menjadi unit kecil yang benar-benar dibeli rumah tangga.

segments.src: - **Assortment** — The mix a retailer carries, described by *breadth* (how many categories) and *depth* (how many choices within one).
segments.tr: - **Berbagai macam (Assortment)** — Campuran yang dibawa oleh pengecer, dijelaskan oleh *kedalaman* (berapa banyak kategori) dan *kedalaman* (berapa banyak pilihan di dalamnya).

segments.src: - **Wheel of Retailing** — McNair's theory that formats enter cheap and no-frills, gradually add cost and service, and are displaced by the next low-price entrant.
segments.tr: - **Roda Ritel (Wheel of Retailing)** — Teori McNair bahwa format masuk dengan murah dan tanpa embel-embel, secara bertahap menambahkan biaya dan layanan, dan digantikan oleh pendatang harga rendah berikutnya.

segments.src: - **Omnichannel** — Running stores, web, app, and delivery as one integrated system rather than separate businesses.
segments.tr: - **Omnichannel** — Menjalankan toko, web, aplikasi, dan pengiriman sebagai satu sistem terintegrasi daripada bisnis terpisah.

segments.src: **2) X (False)** — the margin pays for bulk-breaking, assortment, inventory risk, store hours, and returns; a supermarket's net profit is typically only about 1–3 cents on the dollar.

ja.title: [小売入門 #4] ラスト100フィート：店舗が今なおすべてを決める理由

segments.src: > Retailing is the final step that moves a product from a business to a person who will actually use it — and that step does far more work than "buy low, sell high."
segments.tr: > 小売とは、製品を企業から実際に使用する個人へと移動させる最終段階であり、その段階は「安く買って高く売る」以上のことをはるかに多く行っています。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: **Retailing is the sale of goods and services to final consumers for their own personal use — not for resale, and not as an input into another business's product.**
segments.tr: **小売とは、転売目的ではなく、また他社の製品のインプットとしてもなく、最終消費者が個人的に使用するための財およびサービスの販売です。**

segments.src: That one sentence carries the whole definition.
segments.tr: その一文にすべての定義が詰まっています。

segments.src: When a steel mill sells sheet steel to an automaker, that is not retailing; the steel goes into a car.
segments.tr: 製鉄所が自動車メーカーに鋼板を販売する場合、それは小売ではありません。その鋼鉄は車の一部になります。

segments.src: When you buy a set of floor mats for that car at an auto parts store, that *is* retailing.
segments.tr: 自動車部品店でその車のフロアマットセットを購入する場合、それは*まさに*小売です。

segments.src: The test is not the size of the seller or whether there's a physical store.
segments.tr: テストとなるのは、売り手の規模や実店舗の有無ではありません。

segments.src: It's who the buyer is and why they're buying.
segments.tr: 買い手が誰であり、なぜ買っているかです。

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer.
segments.tr: Amazonは小売業者です。

segments.src: So is the food truck downtown, the dentist's office, and the barbershop — services count too.
segments.tr: 街中のフードトラック、歯医者のオフィス、理髪店も同様です。サービスも小売に含まれます。

segments.src: Retail is also the last link in what textbooks call the **distribution channel**: producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer.
segments.tr: 小売はまた、教科書で**流通チャネル**と呼ばれるものの最後のリンクでもあります。生産者 → 卸売業者 → 小売業者 → 消費者。

segments.src: Being last sounds unglamorous, but it's where a specific set of jobs gets done that nobody upstream wants to do:
segments.tr: 最後尾であることは華やかさがないように聞こえますが、そこは誰も上流でやりたがらない特定の仕事が完了する場所です。

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk.** A roaster ships coffee by the pallet. You want one 12-ounce bag. Someone has to break a pallet into bags, and eat the cost of doing it.
segments.tr: - **大口分割（ブレーキング・バルク）。** ロースターはコーヒーをパレット単位で出荷します。あなたは12オンスのバッグを1つ欲しています。誰かがパレットをバッグに分解し、そのコストを引き受ける必要があります。

segments.src: - **Building an assortment.** No manufacturer makes everything you need for dinner. A supermarket assembles 30,000-plus items from thousands of suppliers into one trip.
segments.tr: - **品揃えの構築。** ディナーに必要なものすべてを製造するメーカーはありません。スーパーマーケットは数千のサプライヤーから3万以上の品目を集め、1度の買い物で揃えられるようにします。

segments.src: - **Holding inventory.** The retailer buys and owns the product *before* knowing if it will sell. That's real financial risk, sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: - **在庫の保持。** 小売業者は、売れるかどうか分からない*前に*製品を購入し、所有します。それは棚に置かれた状態での実際の財務的リスクです。

segments.src: - **Providing services.** Store hours, parking, returns, credit, delivery, installation, someone who can answer "will this fit my sink?"
segments.tr: - **サービスの提供。** 店舗の営業時間、駐車場、返品、クレジット、配達、設置、「これは私のシンクに合いますか？」に答えられるスタッフ。

segments.src: - **Sending information both ways.** Prices and product info flow down to you; scanner data and demand signals flow back up to manufacturers.
segments.tr: - **双方向の情報送信。** 価格や製品情報はあなたに流れ、スキャナーデータや需要シグナルはメーカーへと流れ戻ります。

segments.src: Economists describe this as creating **utility**: *place* utility (the good is where you are), *time* utility (available when you want it), *possession* utility (ownership transfers easily), and *form* utility (bulk becomes a usable size).
segments.tr: 経済学者はこれを**効用**の創造と表現します。*場所*の効用（商品があなたのいる場所にある）、*時間*の効用（欲しいときに利用できる）、*所有*の効用（所有権が簡単に移転する）、そして*形態*の効用（バルクが使用可能なサイズになる）。

segments.src: None of it is free, and all of it is why retail markups exist.
segments.tr: そのどれもが無料ではなく、そのすべてが小売りのマークアップが存在する理由です。

segments.src: **How we got here** — a fast tour of U.S.
segments.tr: **私たちがここに至った経緯** — 米国の

segments.src: retail history, because each format was an answer to a problem:
segments.tr: 小売の歴史の簡単なツアー。それぞれのフォーマットが問題に対する答えだったからです。

segments.src: - **1800s — general stores and peddlers.** Small assortments, negotiated prices, credit written in a ledger.
segments.tr: - **1800年代 — 一般雑貨店と行商。** 小規模な品揃え、交渉による価格、台帳に記録されたクレジット。

segments.src: - **1850s–1870s — department stores.** Macy's (1858) and peers introduced fixed prices, wide assortments under one roof, and returns.
segments.tr: - **1850年代〜1870年代 — 百貨店。** メイシーズ（1858年）とその仲間たちが固定価格、1つの屋根の下での幅広い品揃え、返品を導入しました。

segments.src: - **1872–1893 — mail order.** Montgomery Ward and then Sears used the railroad and the postal service to reach farm households with a catalog. Sound familiar?
segments.tr: - **1872年〜1893年 — 通信販売。** モンゴメリー・ワード、そしてシアーズが鉄道と郵便サービスを利用してカタログで農家へとアプローチしました。聞き覚えがありますか？

segments.src: - **1916 — self-service.** Piggly Wiggly in Memphis let shoppers pick items off shelves themselves, cutting labor cost sharply.
segments.tr: - **1916年 — セルフサービス。** メンフィスのピッグリー・ウィグリーは、買い物客が自分で棚から商品を選べるようにし、人件費を大幅に削減しました。

segments.src: - **1930 — supermarkets.** King Kullen in Queens combined self-service, scale, and parking.
segments.tr: - **1930年 — スーパーマーケット。** クイーンズのキング・カレンは、セルフサービス、規模、駐車場を組み合わせました。

segments.src: - **1962 — discount stores.** Walmart, Kmart, and Target all opened their first stores that same year, trading service for low price.
segments.tr: - **1962年 — ディスカウントストア。** ウォルマート、Kマート、ターゲットが同年に最初の店舗を開業し、サービスを犠牲にして低価格を追求しました。

segments.src: - **1980s–1990s — category killers and warehouse clubs.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: go extremely deep in one category, win on price and selection.
segments.tr: - **1980年代〜1990年代 — カテゴリーキラーと会員制倉庫型店舗。** ホームデポ、ベストバイ、コストコ：1つのカテゴリーを極限まで深掘りし、価格と品揃えで勝利しました。

segments.src: - **1994 onward — e-commerce and omnichannel.** Amazon launched in the mid-1990s; today online is roughly 16–17% of total U.S. retail sales, and most large chains blend the two (buy online, pick up in store).
segments.tr: - **1994年以降 — Eコマンスとオムニチャネル。** Amazonは1990年中盤に立ち上げられ、今日ではオンラインは米国の総小売売上高のおよそ16〜17%を占め、ほとんどの大手チェーンがその2つを融合させています（オンラインで買い、店舗で受け取る）。

de.title: [Einzelhandel 101 #4] Die letzten 30 Meter: Warum das Geschäft immer noch alles entscheidet

segments.src: > Retailing is the final step that moves a product from a business to a person who will actually use it — and that step does far more work than "buy low, sell high."
segments.tr: > Der Einzelhandel ist der letzte Schritt, der ein Produkt von einem Unternehmen zu einer Person bringt, die es tatsächlich nutzen wird – und dieser Schritt leistet weit mehr Arbeit als nur "günstig einkaufen, teuer verkaufen."

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: **Retailing is the sale of goods and services to final consumers for their own personal use — not for resale, and not as an input into another business's product.**
segments.tr: **Einzelhandel ist der Verkauf von Waren und Dienstleistungen an Endverbraucher für deren persönlichen Gebrauch – nicht zum Wiederverkauf und nicht als Vorleistung für das Produkt eines anderen Unternehmens.**

segments.src: That one sentence carries the whole definition.
segments.tr: Dieser eine Satz enthält die gesamte Definition.

segments.src: When a steel mill sells sheet steel to an automaker, that is not retailing; the steel goes into a car.
segments.tr: Wenn ein Stahlwerk Stahlblech an einen Autohersteller verkauft, ist das kein Einzelhandel; der Stahl fließt in ein Auto ein.

segments.src: When you buy a set of floor mats for that car at an auto parts store, that *is* retailing.
segments.tr: Wenn Sie in einem Autoteilegeschäft einen Satz Fußmatten für dieses Auto kaufen, *ist* das Einzelhandel.

segments.src: The test is not the size of the seller or whether there's a physical store.
segments.tr: Der Test ist nicht die Größe des Verkäufers oder ob es ein physisches Geschäft gibt.

segments.src: It's who the buyer is and why they're buying.
segments.tr: Es geht darum, wer der Käufer ist und warum er kauft.

segments.src: Amazon is a retailer.
segments.tr: Amazon ist ein Einzelhändler.

segments.src: So is the food truck downtown, the dentist's office, and the barbershop — services count too.
segments.tr: Das gilt auch für den Imbisswagen in der Innenstadt, die Zahnarztpraxis und den Friseursalon – Dienstleistungen zählen ebenfalls dazu.

segments.src: Retail is also the last link in what textbooks call the **distribution channel**: producer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer.
segments.tr: Der Einzelhandel ist auch das letzte Glied in der sogenannten **Vertriebskette**: Hersteller → Großhändler → Einzelhändler → Verbraucher.

segments.src: Being last sounds unglamorous, but it's where a specific set of jobs gets done that nobody upstream wants to do:
segments.tr: Als Letzter dazustehen klingt wenig glamourös, aber hier werden spezifische Aufgaben erledigt, die niemand weiter oben in der Kette übernehmen will:

segments.src: - **Breaking bulk.** A roaster ships coffee by the pallet. You want one 12-ounce bag. Someone has to break a pallet into bags, and eat the cost of doing it.
segments.tr: - **Mengenauflösung (Breaking Bulk).** Ein Röster versendet Kaffee palettenweise. Sie möchten eine 12-Unzen-Packung. Jemand muss eine Palette in Packungen aufteilen und die Kosten dafür tragen.

segments.src: - **Building an assortment.** No manufacturer makes everything you need for dinner. A supermarket assembles 30,000-plus items from thousands of suppliers into one trip.
segments.tr: - **Zusammenstellung eines Sortiments.** Kein Hersteller produziert alles, was Sie für das Abendessen brauchen. Ein Supermarkt stellt 30.000 plus Artikel von tausenden Lieferanten für einen einzigen Einkauf zusammen.

segments.src: - **Holding inventory.** The retailer buys and owns the product *before* knowing if it will sell. That's real financial risk, sitting on a shelf.
segments.tr: - **Lagerhaltung.** Der Einzelhändler kauft und besitzt das Produkt, *bevor* er weiß, ob es sich verkaufen wird. Das ist ein echtes finanzielles Risiko, das im Regal liegt.

segments.src: - **Providing services.** Store hours, parking, returns, credit, delivery, installation, someone who can answer "will this fit my sink?"
segments.tr: - **Erbringung von Dienstleistungen.** Öffnungszeiten, Parkplätze, Rückgaben, Kredit, Lieferung, Installation, jemand, der die Frage beantworten kann: "Passt das in mein Waschbecken?"

segments.src: - **Sending information both ways.** Prices and product info flow down to you; scanner data and demand signals flow back up to manufacturers.
segments.tr: - **Informationsfluss in beide Richtungen.** Preise und Produktinformationen fließen zu Ihnen; Scannerdaten und Nachfragesignale fließen zurück zu den Herstellern.

segments.src: Economists describe this as creating **utility**: *place* utility (the good is where you are), *time* utility (available when you want it), *possession* utility (ownership transfers easily), and *form* utility (bulk becomes a usable size).
segments.tr: Ökonomen beschreiben dies als die Schaffung von **Nutzen**: *Ort*-Nutzen (die Ware ist dort, wo Sie sind), *Zeit*-Nutzen (verfügbar, wenn Sie sie wollen), *Besitz*-Nutzen (Eigentumsübertragung erfolgt einfach) und *Form*-Nutzen (Massenware wird in eine nutzbare Größe gebracht).

segments.src: None of it is free, and all of it is why retail markups exist.
segments.tr: Nichts davon ist kostenlos, und all das ist der Grund, warum es Einzelhandelsaufschläge gibt.

segments.src: **How we got here** — a fast tour of U.S.
segments.tr: **Wie wir hierher gekommen sind** — ein Schnelldurchlauf durch die Geschichte des US-Einzelhandels,

segments.src: retail history, because each format was an answer to a problem:
segments.tr: denn jedes Format war eine Antwort auf ein Problem:

segments.src: - **1800s — general stores and peddlers.** Small assortments, negotiated prices, credit written in a ledger.
segments.tr: - **1800er — Gemischtwarenläden und Hausierer.** Kleine Sortimente, ausgehandelte Preise, Kredit in einem Buch geführt.

segments.src: - **1850s–1870s — department stores.** Macy's (1858) and peers introduced fixed prices, wide assortments under one roof, and returns.
segments.tr: - **1850er–1870er — Kaufhäuser.** Macy's (1858) und andere führten Festpreise, breite Sortimente unter einem Dach und Rückgabemöglichkeiten ein.

segments.src: - **1872–1893 — mail order.** Montgomery Ward and then Sears used the railroad and the postal service to reach farm households with a catalog. Sound familiar?
segments.tr: - **1872–1893 — Versandhandel.** Montgomery Ward und später Sears nutzten die Eisenbahn und den Postdienst, um landwirtschaftliche Haushalte mit einem Katalog zu erreichen. Kommt Ihnen das bekannt vor?

segments.src: - **1916 — self-service.** Piggly Wiggly in Memphis let shoppers pick items off shelves themselves, cutting labor cost sharply.
segments.tr: - **1916 — Selbstbedienung.** Piggly Wiggly in Memphis ließ die Kunden die Waren selbst aus den Regalen nehmen, was die Arbeitskosten drastisch senkte.

segments.src: - **1930 — supermarkets.** King Kullen in Queens combined self-service, scale, and parking.
segments.tr: - **1930 — Supermärkte.** King Kullen in Queens kombinierte Selbstbedienung, Größe und Parkplätze.

segments.src: - **1962 — discount stores.** Walmart, Kmart, and Target all opened their first stores that same year, trading service for low price.
segments.tr: - **1962 — Discounter.** Walmart, Kmart und Target eröffneten alle im selben Jahr ihre ersten Geschäfte und tauschten Service gegen niedrige Preise.

segments.src: - **1980s–1990s — category killers and warehouse clubs.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: go extremely deep in one category, win on price and selection.
segments.tr: - **1980er–1990er — Category Killer und Lagerhaus-Clubs.** Home Depot, Best Buy, Costco: extrem tiefes Sortiment in einer Kategorie, Gewinn durch Preis und Auswahl.

segments.src: - **1994 onward — e-commerce and omnichannel.** Amazon launched in the mid-1990s; today online is roughly 16–17% of total U.S. retail sales, and most large chains blend the two (buy online, pick up in store).
segments.tr: - **1994 bis heute — E-Commerce und Omnichannel.** Amazon startete Mitte der 1990er Jahre; heute macht der Online-Handel etwa 16–17 % des gesamten US-Einzelhandelsumsatzes aus, und die meisten großen Ketten kombinieren beides (online kaufen, im Geschäft abholen).

segments.src: Notice the pattern.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie das Muster.

segments.src: Malcolm McNair called it the **Wheel of Retailing**: new formats usually enter as low-price, low-margin, no-frills operators, gradually add services and costs as they mature, and thereby open the low end for the next disruptor.
segments.tr: Malcolm McNair nannte es das **Rad des Einzelhandels (Wheel of Retailing)**: Neue Formate treten normalerweise als Anbieter mit niedrigen Preisen, geringen Margen und ohne Schnickschnack ein, fügen mit zunehmender Reife nach und nach Dienstleistungen und Kosten hinzu und öffnen dadurch das untere Ende für den nächsten Disruptor.

segments.src: Discounters did it to department stores.
segments.tr: Discounter taten dies bei Kaufhäusern.

segments.src: Online did it to discounters.
segments.tr: Online-Händler taten dies bei Discountern.

segments.src: Something will do it to online.
segments.tr: Etwas wird dies auch bei Online-Händlern tun.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: You pay **$12.99** for a 12-ounce bag of coffee at a Kroger in Columbus on a Sunday evening.
segments.tr: Sie zahlen **$12.99** für eine 12-Unzen-Packung Kaffee bei einem Kroger in Columbus an einem Sonntagabend.

segments.src: It feels like a small transaction.
segments.tr: Es fühlt sich wie eine kleine Transaktion an.

segments.src: Count what the store actually did for that price.
segments.tr: Zählen Sie mal, was das Geschäft für diesen Preis tatsächlich getan hat.

segments.src: The beans were grown in Colombia, sold in 60-kilogram sacks, shipped in a container, roasted in a facility that runs in thousand-pound batches, and trucked to a distribution center on a pallet holding a couple hundred bags.
segments.tr: Die Bohnen wurden in Kolumbien angebaut, in 60-Kilogramm-Säcken verkauft, in einem Container verschifft, in einer Anlage geröstet, die in Tausend-Pfund-Chargen arbeitet, und auf einer Palette mit ein paar hundert Packungen zu einem Verteilzentrum gefahren.

segments.src: The retailer bought that pallet outright — before knowing whether Columbus would want medium roast this month.
segments.tr: Der Einzelhändler kaufte diese Palette direkt – bevor er wusste, ob Columbus diesen Monat mittlere Röstung wollte.

segments.src: It broke the pallet into single bags, put them on a shelf next to eleven competing brands plus whole-bean, ground, and decaf options, kept the lights and the doors open until 10 p.m., took your card, and would have refunded you without argument if the bag was stale.
segments.tr: Er teilte die Palette in einzelne Packungen auf, stellte sie in ein Regal neben elf konkurrierende Marken sowie ganze Bohnen, gemahlenen Kaffee und entkoffeinierte Optionen, hielt das Licht an und die Türen bis 22 Uhr offen, nahm Ihre Karte und hätte Ihnen das Geld ohne Diskussion zurückerstattet, wenn die Packung abgestanden gewesen wäre.

segments.src: For all of that, a typical U.S.
segments.tr: Für all das behält ein typischer US-Supermarkt

segments.src: supermarket keeps roughly **1 to 3 cents of net profit per dollar** of sales.
segments.tr: etwa **1 bis 3 Cent Nettogewinn pro Dollar** Umsatz.

segments.src: Groceries are one of the thinnest-margin businesses in the country.
segments.tr: Lebensmittelgeschäfte gehören zu den Unternehmen mit den geringsten Margen im Land.

segments.src: The gap between what the store paid and what you paid mostly went to rent, wages, refrigeration, trucks, shrink, and unsold inventory — that is, to the cost of getting one bag of coffee within walking distance of your kitchen at a moment you chose.
segments.tr: Die Differenz zwischen dem, was das Geschäft bezahlt hat, und dem, was Sie bezahlt haben, floss größtenteils in Miete, Löhne, Kühlung, LKWs, Schwund und unverkauftes Inventar – das heißt, in die Kosten dafür, eine Packung Kaffee in Laufnähe zu Ihrer Küche zu einem Zeitpunkt Ihrer Wahl zu bekommen.

segments.src: That's the honest answer to "why not just buy direct from the roaster?"
segments.tr: Das ist die ehrliche Antwort auf die Frage: "Warum nicht einfach direkt beim Röster kaufen?"

segments.src: You can.
segments.tr: Das können Sie.

segments.src: You'll wait three days, pay shipping, and commit before tasting it.
segments.tr: Sie warten drei Tage, zahlen Versandkosten und legen sich fest, bevor Sie ihn probiert haben.

segments.src: The store's price includes the option of changing your mind.
segments.tr: Der Preis des Geschäfts beinhaltet die Option, Ihre Meinung zu ändern.
